Simulate related chromatograms with shared compound spectra

Source: R/simulateGCMSSamples.R
simulateGCMSSamples.Rd

Generate exponentially modified Gaussian and optional triangular acid peaks, smooth backgrounds, irregular scan grids, sample drift and concentration- dependent peak widths and tails. Missing compounds can be simulated explicitly.

Usage

simulateGCMSSamples(
  samples = 3L,
  n = 600L,
  k = 26L,
  S = NULL,
  preset = c("time_area_acid", "same", "time", "time_area"),
  presence = 1,
  absent = NULL,
  irregular = 0.12,
  drift = 2,
  area = 2e+05,
  seed = 811,
  width_time = 0.5,
  width_area = 0.45,
  tail_time = 1,
  tail_area = 1.5,
  rt_area = 0.25,
  acid_fraction = 0.08,
  family = c("poisson", "quasipoisson", "nb", "gaussian", "Gamma", "nb1", "Gamma_scale"),
  dispersion = 1,
  theta = 20,
  retentionIndex = NULL,
  retentionMap = NULL,
  background = NULL
)

Arguments

samples

Number of samples.

n

Number of scans, recycled across samples.

k

Number of distinct compounds.

S

Optional spectral library with one compound per row.

preset

Peak-shape scenario: identical shapes, time-dependent shapes, time and concentration-dependent shapes, or the latter with acid peaks.

presence

Probability that each compound occurs in each sample.

absent

Optional logical compounds-by-samples absence matrix.

irregular

Relative scan-width variation, from zero to 0.5.

drift

Drift per sample, in seconds.

area

Typical integrated compound intensity.

seed

Random-number seed.

width_time, width_area, tail_time, tail_area, rt_area

Effects of time and concentration on peak width, tail and retention time.

acid_fraction

Fraction of broad triangular acid profiles.

family

Signal distribution name supported by logconNMF().

dispersion, theta

Noise parameters.

retentionIndex

Optional retention indices, one per row of S. When retentionMap is supplied, the default is the positional RI attribute of the spectral library.

retentionMap

Optional calibration data frame with increasing ri and time columns. Times are reference retention times in minutes. Compound locations follow this map and sample drift warps the map for each injection. Each sample returns its known calibration.

background

Optional nonnegative baseline intensity per unit exposure: a scalar, one value per mass channel, or a reference-time-by-channel matrix. Matrix rows are interpolated across the reference chromatogram for each sample's scan grid. The default uses a random low-dimensional spline.

Value

Simulation truth and a list of samples with observations, original bin edges and times (minutes), integrated-count means, true spectra, profiles, areas, presence indicators and acquisition dates. A simulated observation is integrated over its bin; raw_exposure is the original bin duration in seconds. For logconNMF(), supply it as exposure. With retentionMap, each sample includes retentionIndex and an increasing retentionCalibration table incorporating its known drift. The onset field records concentration-adjusted leading positions on the reference time grid; the sample drift then maps them to observed time.

Details

In concentration-dependent scenarios, peak width and tail increase with concentration while the leading 1%-height position stays approximately fixed. The rt_area coefficient optionally adds a small concentration- dependent shift to that position. Triangular acid profiles broaden towards later times from a fixed leading edge. With a single acid profile it is placed in the middle of the chromatogram.

See also

logconNMF(), simulateGCMS()

Examples

sim <- simulateGCMSSamples(samples=3L,n=c(180L,190L,200L),k=8L,
  presence=0.5,seed=3)
sim$present
